findings.text: Capability word 20 uses numeric base 640 with sparse low offsets. Offsets 0 and 1 and 2 cover missing nested data breakpoints, non serializing writes to segment bases, and serializing fence behavior for timestamp reads. Offsets 4 through 6 cover a fixed TLB synchronization erratum, a VERW based transient scheduler mitigation, and base clearing on null selectors. Offsets 8 and 9 cover automatic branch protection and absence of a system management control register, with gaps at 3 and 7.

Upper part of word 20 keeps base 640 with offsets 17 then 20 then 23 and 24 then 27 through 31. They respectively signal faulting on user CPUID, prefetch to cache levels, bit matrix multiply extensions, stronger return predictor isolation, selective branch prediction barrier, IBPB flushing across branch types, two not affected conditions for SRSO including user kernel boundary, and a branch configuration control usable to mitigate SRSO for virtual machines.

Capability word 21 uses base 672 with dense low offsets 0 through 10. They signal freezing of branch and counter state, software loop clearing of branch history at system call entry and at virtual machine exit, availability and enablement of hardware control for that clearing, fast power cooperation, heterogeneous core topology, workload classification, avoidance of wide vectors, advanced performance extensions, and thunks for indirect branches in the lower half of a cache line.

Upper offsets 11 through 20 of word 21 continue from base 672. They signal non vulnerability to two scheduler attack variants, clearing of CPU buffers before virtual entry in general and in a host MMIO conditional form that is redundant when the general form is set, IBPB on exit to user for a virtual escape issue, assignable bandwidth monitoring, immediate forms of system register instructions, enclave version update support, smart cache injection enforcement, and extended virtual interrupt support for large virtual CPU counts.

Bug identifiers are formed by adding a small index to a base derived from the capability word count times 32. Indices 0 through 12 denote legacy faults and errata: lock prefix hang, divide flaw, coma hang, TLB mismatch, APIC power interaction, defective APIC, register save leakage, required flush before monitor, SYSRET segment attributes, IRET stack width corruption, selector base preservation, SWAPGS ordering hazard, and need for inter processor wakeup.

Bug indices 13 through 25 continue the same base and denote erratum 400 membership plus meltdown, two Spectre variants, store bypass, terminal fault, microarchitectural sampling with a sampling only variant, SWAPGS speculation, async abort, multihit machine check risk, random number leakage, and stale MMIO data. Indices 27 through 31 skip 26 and denote return misprediction leakage, post barrier prediction weakness, cross thread return prediction, gather sampling, and partial write machine check risk for confidential guests.

A second bug word starts at base plus 32 and uses sub offsets 0 through 12. They denote SRSO, divide by zero speculation, register file sampling, branch history injection, IBPB omitting return targets, user to user Spectre variant 2, old microcode, indirect target selection with a native only variant, transient scheduler attacks, virtual escape from guests, seam return clearing virtual control state, and a TLB invalidation erratum.

Inline query helpers expose processor identification without locking. A predicate always reports CPUID availability, a raw wrapper exchanges four register values with two inputs, generated readers return one register for a leaf with cleared subleaf, generic helpers read a leaf with cleared subleaf into caller registers, and indexed helpers read a leaf plus subleaf into a four word array or extract one indexed register with compile time size enforcement for 16 byte and 4 byte destinations.

Dispatch separates plain leaves from indexed leaves. Indexed leaves comprise decimal 4 and 7 and 11 and 13, then 15 and 16 and 18 and 20, then 23 and 24 and 29 and 30 and 31, then 36 and an extended topology leaf. Callers clear the subleaf input to avoid stale values on parts that leave ECX untouched, the raw wrapper treats memory as clobbered, and builds with paravirt redirect the generic path while direct readers keep using the raw instruction.

Leaf 2 output is normalized before interpretation. An iteration count other than one causes all outputs to be treated as empty, each register whose invalid indicator is set is cleared independently, and descriptor iteration walks bytes 1 through 15 while translating each byte through a shared descriptor table.

Vendor leaf layout holds four 32 bit words. The first word gives the highest standard leaf, while the remaining three words carry the twelve byte vendor identifier split as bytes 0 to 3 and 8 to 11 and 4 to 7 across the second, third, and fourth words respectively.

Version and feature leaf layout packs identification and capability flags into four words. The first word holds stepping, base and extended model and family, and processor type. The second word holds brand, flush line size, logical processor count, and initial APIC identity. The third and fourth words each hold 32 single bit capability indicators for instruction, virtualization, power, debug, and platform features.

Cache descriptor leaf layout holds an iteration count plus fifteen descriptor bytes across four words. Each word reserves its top bit as an invalid marker for the descriptors carried in that word, so setting the marker discards the associated group while leaving other groups intact.

Parsed CPUID state is accessed through const views keyed by leaf and subleaf. Single subleaf access returns a pointer only when exactly one entry was filled, indexed access validates the requested subleaf against a per leaf first subleaf plus range size and against the filled count and otherwise yields nothing, range size comes from the static array extent, checks enforce multi entry ranges and constant subleaf bounds, raw views reinterpret typed leaves as register quadruples, a count helper reports filled indexed entries, and AMD style L3 presence is inferred from any nonzero extended leaf 6 EDX value.

Several inputs must be treated as untrusted or incomplete. Leaf 2 may report bogus iteration counts or invalid registers and must be sanitized, some parts leave ECX unchanged so callers must preset it, the parser may fill only a prefix of an indexed range so callers must handle absent entries, descriptor translation depends on an external table, and the AMD L3 predicate is only a nonzero test rather than a decoded field.

The raw CPUID instruction wrapper is the architectural boundary for all direct queries in this lane. It accepts leaf in EAX with subleaf in ECX through caller memory, issues the identifying instruction, returns EAX EBX ECX EDX through the same memory, and is reused by single register and array helpers.
Both CPUID headers use include guards that define a unique macro on first inclusion so repeated inclusion within one translation unit has no effect.
